topic: Inadvertent hypothermia in critically ill patients
standard: NICE guidance on inadvertent hypothermia (temperature under 36C): at least 4-hourly temperature observations, no patient inadvertently hypothermic, all hypothermic patients rewarmed
finding: 29% of patients had at least 4-hourly temperatures; 1.4 overdue observations per day; 24% became hypothermic, for a mean 7.9 hours; intervention documented in 15% (2931 patient-hours).
change: Simple education programme and a departmental protocol for prevention and management of inadvertent hypothermia.

detail.setting: Intensive care unit, Freeman Hospital, Newcastle upon Tyne

cycle1.result: 29% of patients had at least 4-hourly temperatures; 1.4 overdue observations per day; 24% became hypothermic, for a mean 7.9 hours; intervention documented in 15% (2931 patient-hours).

detail.intervention: Simple education programme and a departmental protocol for prevention and management of inadvertent hypothermia.

cycle2.result: 40% had at least 4-hourly temperatures (p<0.01); 0.9 overdue observations per day (p<0.01); 22% became hypothermic (p=0.07) for a mean 6.1 hours (p<0.01); intervention documented in 46% (p<0.001) (2070 patient-hours).

standard: Local ITU guidelines on routine blood tests and blood volume taken
finding: 901 patient-days: U&E and FBC requested in line with guidelines; LFT, bone profile, magnesium and clotting screen about four times more than advocated; twice the recommended blood volume taken (almost 16 litres); cost 11,019 euros.

detail.setting: Adult intensive therapy unit, ABMU Health Board, Swansea

cycle1.result: 901 patient-days: U&E and FBC requested in line with guidelines; LFT, bone profile, magnesium and clotting screen about four times more than advocated; twice the recommended blood volume taken (almost 16 litres); cost 11,019 euros.

title: Audit of the diagnosis and treatment of seborrhoeic keratosis and compliance with current guidelines.
topic: Dermatoscopy and biopsy method for seborrhoeic keratosis
standard: NICE quality standard for skin cancer: pigmented lesions assessed by specialist must be examined with a dermatoscope; BMJ Best Practice: SK diagnosed clinically, removed by curettage, cautery or cryotherapy, and excision biopsy avoided. No numerical target stated.
finding: Dermatoscopy coded for 28 of 55 patients with available notes (not coded in 49%) and mentioned in 8 of 53 clinic letters. Biopsy method for biopsy-proven SKs: 37 excision, 9 curettage and cautery, 8 shave excision, 8 punch biopsy. 42.9% of patients correctly diagnosed as SK still had an excision biopsy.

detail.setting: Plastic surgery department, St George's Hospital, London

cycle1.result: Dermatoscopy coded for 28 of 55 patients with available notes (not coded in 49%) and mentioned in 8 of 53 clinic letters. Biopsy method for biopsy-proven SKs: 37 excision, 9 curettage and cautery, 8 shave excision, 8 punch biopsy. 42.9% of patients correctly diagnosed as SK still had an excision biopsy.

detail.other_findings: Similar rates of incorrect management between consultants and specialist registrars. Many patients had a significant skin cancer history (33 melanoma), which may have raised suspicion.
detail.citation: Garner J, Sindali K, Powell PBWEM. Audit of the diagnosis and treatment of seborrhoeic keratosis and compliance with current guidelines. JPRAS Open. 2020;26:76-79. doi:10.1016/j.jpra.2020.10.001. PMID: 33195787.
